focus: Recommended path and the build steps a later phase would take (Q5)

label: Recommend Path B: new checker of compiledRoute() decisions against routing-scenario gold — measures correctness directly on live deps; corpus is alive (262 gold files, 44 playbook dirs across 5 hubs) and new hubs author it in build-out anyway
Restore rejected: ~3,700-line surgical landing + freeze re-owning + path-churn verification, to recover compiled-vs-replay-proxy (router-replay models the router, it is not the router)

Keep-closed rejected: converts tooling gap to permanent program freeze — strands ready-mints, blinds admitted-hub drift re-verification, compounds doc debt; only honest alongside an explicit cohort-frozen decision

Bar redefinition must be recorded: 'compiled == authored routing gold, zero violations' replaces 'compiled == legacy replay'; shared-gold-gap blocks (stricter), correct-but-different passes (looser, bounded by completeness gate)

Mitigations: playbook corpus required (canary-cases = smoke only); corpus-completeness gate (every declared mode scored, ungolded modes = violations); defer/holdout/negative counting ported; gold-parse-failure = violation

Build steps: check-compiled-routing.cjs (~500-800 lines: loader+comparator+rollup+completeness gate+report), vitest suite, admission runbook (HUB_CHILD -> checker -> mint/refresh -> flip -> cohort tables -> sync promote -> guard green), doc fixes incl. flip-serving scorer-gate repair and seven->five

Operator decision rule: Path B if new hubs will ever be admitted; restore only if bar must stay literally '== legacy replay' (budget replay+scorer resurrection); closed only with explicit cohort-frozen decision

reason: The fidelity is to a replay proxy, not to legacy itself; the stated-equivalence bar would need the replay+scorer resurrection anyway
It freezes the program rather than protecting it: no new-hub path, no drift re-verification, compounding doc debt
